pages: This story starts at the end of a war and at the foreshawdowing of a massacare...
After ten long year of battle, the Greeks' seemingly defeated sent a great wooden statue to the Trojans as a gift of surrender.
The Trojans, believing the war was over, brought the horse into their city unbeknownst to them Odesseus' deception...
Under the cover of darkness, the Greeks emerged from the horse and opened the gates to their waiting army.
The city that had resisted them for a decade was overwhelmed in a single night
And what followed is described by poets a most brutal massacre
Odysseus and Agamemnon departed from the ruins of the city and set sail for home, having their ships laden with the spoils of war.
Behind them Troy lay shattered and burning and before them the sea...
For Odysseus, the war was finally over but his troubles were only beginning...
Departing seperately from Agamemnon, the voyage soon became a struggle for survival
Storms drove the Greek ships across a merciless sea, tearing at their sails and scattering their men.
Only they knew what horrors they witnessed in their journey...
At last, the sea cast Odysseus upon an unfamiliar shore
Exhausted and broken, he could do nothing but resign himself to the fate the gods had in store for him.
And so Calypso, the nymph of the island, found his lifeless body and took him in to her care...
